verification.note: Read from the product having one load, which its group 1 controls, as on other one-load products.

steps.text: At the circuit breaker or fuse panel, turn off the circuit supplying power to the switch.
Remove the faceplate from the existing switch, unscrew the switch and pull it out of the junction box.
Disconnect the wires from the old switch and make sure you have 1/2 in. of bare wire on the ends.
Turn the power back on.
Identify the line, load, neutral and ground wires with a voltage meter.
Turn the breaker off again.

Connect the switch's black line wire to line, its red load wire to the load, its white neutral wire to the box's neutral bundle and its bare copper ground wire to ground. A neutral connection is required.
Make sure all wire connectors are firmly attached and no copper is exposed except the ground wire.
Orient the switch with the LED bar at the left, place it in the junction box and screw it into place.
Turn the power back on at the circuit breaker or fuse panel.
Test the switch by using the paddle to turn the light on and off.
Reinstall the faceplate.

notes: If there is no neutral wire in the box, consult an electrician.

In a virtual multi-way circuit only the primary switch connects to the load; secondaries connect to line, neutral and ground and their red load wire is capped. The On/Off Switch 2476S Owner's Manual gives the full multi-way wiring.
Pull the SET button out about 1/8 in. to open the air gap and remove all power from the switch and its load; push it back in flush to restore power.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps (about 3 seconds).
steps.expect: Status LED blinks; the switch stays in linking mode for four minutes

notes: As a controller: put the switch in linking mode first, set the responder to the desired state, then press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds; the switch double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.

As a responder: put the controller in linking mode first, set the load with the paddle, then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps (about 3 seconds); the status LED flashes once, then turns on solid.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps (about 3 seconds).
steps.expect: Status LED blinks; the switch stays in linking mode for four minutes

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder; the device makes no link back to the Hub, since this profile lists no group it controls.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, set it to the desired state.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it beeps or its LED flashes.
After adding all responders, tap the SET button.
Test by tapping the switch on and off a couple of times.
Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps (about 3 seconds).
Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps again (about 3 seconds).
steps.expect: Status LED keeps blinking; the switch stays in unlinking mode for four minutes

notes: As a controller: after entering unlinking mode, press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds; the switch double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.
As a responder: put the controller in unlinking mode first, then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps; the status LED flashes once, then turns on solid.

To remove several responders in one session, tap the SET button after entering unlinking mode (LED double-blinks), press and hold each responder's SET button until it beeps, then tap the SET button to finish.

steps.text: Pull out the SET button to open the air gap.
Wait 10 seconds.
Push in the SET button and hold it; do not let go.
When the beep stops, release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the switch double-beeps, the LEDs return to normal brightness and the load turns on

steps.text: Unlink the switch from every controller that controls it.
Unlink every responder the switch controls.

notes: The On/Off Switch 2476S Owner's Manual says to unlink the switch from all controllers before disabling or removing it, and to unlink responders before they are removed, otherwise devices keep retrying commands and delay the network.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove the modem's group 0 link with no SET button press: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09). This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as the On/Off Switch 2476S Owner's Manual gives it, clears them. This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.
